profile.headline: Computer Science and Software Engineer Grad | Impacting society through technology
profile.summary:
When I was a boy, I wanted be a video game designer. I loved the graphics, the concepts; playing them made me want to share the joy I was experiencing. In fact, I began writing a lot of short stories around my age filled with lots creativity to be later used as a storyline. When I hit 8th grade I got a feel for my desire. I did a summer program called youth digital studios where we designed a two way platform game using javascript as the programming language. After that I was ecstatic to the idea of programming. I continued this career path in high school, joining a programing class where we coded the IDE netbeans language java.We created several projects, the biggest two were the brick breaker game and a calculator; that involved frontend and backend programming. I went on to do projects myself dealing with math, for an example a program that solves integrals, finds derivatives, and other calculus problems.Now I am currently enrolled in college working towards a Computer Science degree. I am also learning a second coding language C#. I am currently seeking to gain more experience in the world of coding not only to be apart of bettering the world but also bringing happiness 
Also in high school, I joined a graphic design class to build and learn on how to be more expressive with my art. I contended at a competition called SkillUSA and competed at the state level in the category of Promotional bulletin board. As a result me and my teammate got 4th out of 16 people. I also took up an internship for 9 months, with a business that revolves around graphic design during high school. The skills I gained from it, helped me establish my own small clothing line “Clutch Graphics”.

As a volunteer with the Robins SE&TM Junior Force Council (JFC), I support the professional growth of emerging Scientists, Engineers, and Technical Managers at Robins Air Force Base. My role involves facilitating mentorship, networking, and leadership development opportunities while serving as a bridge between junior workforce members and senior leadership. Through this initiative, I help empower future leaders by providing resources, advocacy, and career advancement within the Air Force Sustainment Center (AFSC) and Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC).

projects.title: Commanders Challenge
projects.description:
The Commander’s Challenge, hosted by the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL), focused on developing a frontline defense solution capable of detecting, classifying, and contributing to the defeat of specific unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in operational environments.

I served as the Lead Frontend Developer, Technical Writer, and AI Engineer. I designed and implemented a real-time frontend interface that integrated directly with hardware systems and displayed live data and detection outputs through an interactive visualization dashboard.

In addition to frontend development, I optimized and modified the AI model integrated into our system pipeline to improve performance, reliability, and system interoperability. I ensured seamless communication between hardware components, backend systems, and AI inference outputs.

As one of the team’s technical writer, I authored comprehensive client-side and AI software documentation, detailing system architecture, data flow, model integration, and operational procedures to support maintainability and knowledge transfer.

Our team began with seven members and concluded as a four-person team in the final quarter. Despite reduced manpower, we maintained performance and secured second place among competing teams.

This experience strengthened my expertise in real-time systems integration, AI optimization, hardware-software interfacing, and mission-driven engineering while collaborating with personnel from multiple bases and military branches.

projects.title: Policy Pulse
projects.description: Policy Pulse is a solution to have a periodic monitoring and reporting system to track the activity of onboarded customers' use of UPS Capital's offerings of insurance, delivery defense, and digital solutions. This system consists of a centralized database that stores customer data, Business Development Officers data, transaction data, premium data, state map relation data, support data, and more. Previously, Business Development Officers (BDO) and Customer Success teams could not immediately see their customers and would need to have a convoluted channel of communication to access information. This makes it hard for BDO's and Customer success teams to capture inactive customers. Not only is it hard for the UPSC team, but customers have also claimed that they are not receiving services, and they feel unheard. With the implementation of this database, monthly emails can be sent to specific Business Development Officers who are responsible for certain clientele, and they will receive reports on onboarded customers who are inactive. Further data can be accessed based off region and territory on an interactive map on PowerBI. Having an established way for BDO's and Customer Success workers to find inactive customers will improve customer satisfaction since a direct lane of information will be sent to BDO's and Customer Success.
